title: CSC: Calibrated Simplicity for Conflict-Aware Social Bot Detection in the LLM Era
abstract: arXiv:2609.23320v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Social bot detection is essential for protecting online platforms from misinformation amplification, coordinated manipulation, and distorted public discourse. However, large language models have made social bots much harder to detect from text alone because semantic camouflage is now cheap, fluent, and scalable. The resulting challenge is modality conflict: an account may look human-like in semantics while remaining suspicious in graph structure, profile attributes, or cross-modal consistency. Recent graph-based detectors tackle this limitation by adding graph-side complexity, such as sparse prototype selection, adaptive gating, or architecture-specific control logic, yet our experiments suggest that complexity alone is not the most reliable way to resolve such conflict. translated_title: CSC：面向大语言模型时代的冲突感知社交机器人检测的校准简洁性框架
translated_abstract: 社交机器人检测对于保护在线平台免受虚假信息放大、协同操纵和公共舆论扭曲至关重要。然而，大语言模型使得仅从文本层面检测社交机器人变得困难得多，因为语义伪装如今变得廉价、流畅且可大规模扩展。由此带来的挑战是模态冲突：一个账户在语义上可能看起来像人类，但在图结构、个人资料属性或跨模态一致性方面仍然可疑。近期基于图的检测器通过增加图侧的复杂性来应对这一局限，例如稀疏原型选择、自适应门控或架构特定的控制逻辑，然而我们的实验表明，仅靠复杂性并非解决此类冲突最可靠的方式。因此，我们提出了CSC，一个面向大语言模型时代冲突感知社交机器人检测的校准简洁性框架。该框架结合了三项设计选择：一个简化的...
tldr: 提出CSC框架，通过校准简洁性而非增加复杂性来解决大语言模型时代社交机器人检测中的模态冲突问题，即账户语义上像人类但图结构和跨模态一致性仍可疑的情况。
en_tdlr: CSC is a calibrated-simplicity framework that resolves modality conflicts in LLM-era social bot detection—where accounts appear human-like semantically yet remain suspicious in graph structure and cross-modal consistency—demonstrating that simplicity, rather than added complexity, is the more reliable solution.
